title: Nvidia and AMD shares fall on report of new U.S. ban on AI chip exports to China
summary: Shares of Nvidia Corp. and Advanced Micro Devices Inc. dropped following a report that the Biden administration is considering a new ban on sales of AI chips to China. This potential ban comes despite Nvidia managing to avoid $400 million in lost sales last year after a previous ban on some chip sales to China. The news impacted both companies with Nvidia shares falling 3% after hours and AMD shares also decreasing by 3%.

title: The Cheap Trick Alphabet Is Using To Boost Its Share Price
summary: Alphabet's 20-for-1 stock split, following similar moves by Apple and Tesla, is unlikely to fundamentally change the company's valuation but aims to make shares more accessible to smaller investors and potentially gain entry into the Dow Jones Industrial Average. While some tech giants saw significant share price boosts post-split, Alphabet's future success might be tempered by changing market conditions. The article suggests Amazon could be the next tech giant to undertake a similar split to boost its stock.

title: Nvidia acquires GPU cluster optimization startup Run:ai for reported $700M
summary: Nvidia Corp. has acquired Run:ai, a startup specializing in software that optimizes the performance of graphics card clusters for AI workloads. Although the terms were not officially disclosed, the deal was reportedly valued at $700 million, significantly higher than Run:ai's prior funding. Run:ai's technology aims to boost AI performance by resolving common inefficiencies in GPU-powered servers, such as data exchange delays and memory collisions, allowing for more efficient utilization of GPU resources.

title: Should You Buy Nvidia Stock Before the AI Chipmaker Reports Earnings on May 22?
summary: Nvidia's stock has seen a significant surge due to demand for its GPUs driven by generative AI. With first-quarter earnings approaching on May 22nd, analysts have high expectations for the chipmaker. Investors are advised to be cautious due to the stock's current pricey valuation, despite its strong market position and growth potential in the AI economy.

title: NVIDIA Launches Blackwell-Powered DGX SuperPOD for Generative AI Supercomputing at Trillion-Parameter Scale
summary: NVIDIA has announced its next-generation AI supercomputer, the NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD, powered by GB200 Grace Blackwell Superchips. This new system is designed for processing trillion-parameter models with constant uptime for generative AI training and inference, featuring liquid cooling, 11.5 exaflops of AI supercomputing, and up to 576 Blackwell GPUs. Additionally, NVIDIA unveiled the DGX B200 system, an air-cooled platform for AI model training, fine-tuning, and inference, providing 15x faster real-time inference for trillion-parameter models.

title: Nvidia Faces Investor Scrutiny Over Blackwell Chip Delays, Big Revenue Expected: Report
summary: Nvidia is facing investor scrutiny due to delays in its Blackwell chip rollout, despite expecting "several billion dollars" in revenue from it in the fiscal fourth quarter. The stock has dropped 15% since the announcement, though it remains up over 137% in the last 12 months. Analysts are concerned about the delays in the absence of other positive catalysts, while some argue the selloff is unwarranted given the strong demand for AI technology from Big Tech giants.

title: How Nvidia doubled earnings, lost almost $300 billion in value and shook the stock market
summary: Nvidia experienced a significant stock market shake-up, losing almost $300 billion in value in a single day, despite having doubled its earnings. This downturn is attributed to growing fears of an economic slowdown and renewed skepticism about the immediate payoff from AI investments, causing broader market indexes to also fall. Analysts highlight Nvidia's dependence on continued massive AI investments from major tech companies and warn of stock volatility.

title: How Nvidia Overtook Apple as World's Most Valuable Company
summary: Nvidia briefly surpassed Apple to become the world's most valuable company, driven by the immense demand for its specialized AI chips crucial for advanced AI applications. This shift highlights the growing importance of AI-driven technologies in the tech market, with Nvidia benefiting significantly from the race among tech giants to dominate AI. While Apple later regained its lead, Nvidia's surge underscores the impact of AI on market valuations and investment trends.

title: Nvidia sales grow 78% on AI demand, company gives strong guidance
summary: Nvidia reported strong fiscal fourth-quarter earnings, beating Wall Street expectations, with revenue up 78% year-over-year due to high demand for its AI-accelerating GPUs. The company also issued robust guidance for the first quarter, projecting $43 billion in revenue, driven by the anticipated "significant ramp" of its next-generation Blackwell AI chips. While growth rates are moderating as Nvidia scales, its data center business, now 91% of total sales, continues to surge, with CEO Jensen Huang noting "amazing" demand for Blackwell.

title: NVIDIA to Manufacture American-Made AI Supercomputers in US for First Time
summary: NVIDIA is collaborating with manufacturing partners to produce AI supercomputers entirely within the U.S. for the first time. The company is commissioning over a million square feet of manufacturing space in Arizona and Texas to build and test NVIDIA Blackwell chips and AI supercomputers, aiming to complete up to half a trillion dollars of AI infrastructure in the US within four years. This initiative is expected to create hundreds of thousands of jobs and enhance supply chain resiliency while meeting the growing demand for AI technology.

title: Telcos Across Five Continents Are Building NVIDIA-Powered Sovereign AI Infrastructure | NVIDIA Technical Blog
summary: Telecom companies worldwide are establishing NVIDIA-powered sovereign AI infrastructure to support national AI development and offer GPU-as-a-service. This trend leverages telcos' existing infrastructure, data centers, and expertise, positioning them as trusted providers of AI cloud services to governments, enterprises, and startups. Examples include TELUS in Canada, Cassava Technologies in Africa, and Kazakhtelecom in Central Asia, all building AI factories to drive economic growth and innovation.

title: Nvidia shares hit record as AI chipmaker again becomes world's most valuable company
summary: Nvidia's shares surged, closing at a new record high, driven by investor confidence in its AI leadership despite Chinese export controls. The company is now valued at $3.77 trillion, making it the world's most valuable company. Although China's market is largely closed to Nvidia, its data center business shows significant growth, with analysts projecting 53% revenue growth for the full fiscal year.

title: Nvidia could become a nearly $5 trillion company. Here’s how.
summary: Barclays analysts have raised their price target for Nvidia to $200, indicating a potential 38% increase in its stock price and a market capitalization of nearly $5 trillion. This optimistic outlook is driven by the company's ramp-up of its Blackwell artificial-intelligence platform. Analysts believe Nvidia has the most upside potential among their coverage for the second half of the year.

title: Nvidia is first company worth $5 trillion
summary: Nvidia has become the first company in history to reach a $5 trillion market valuation, driven by the ongoing artificial intelligence investment boom. This milestone comes after rapid growth, with the company reaching $4 trillion just three months prior and $1 trillion a little over two years ago. Despite concerns about a potential AI bubble, Nvidia's CEO Jensen Huang asserts that the companies are generating real, profitable revenues.

title: U.S. Retracts Tariff Waiver for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing
summary: The U.S. Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) has retracted a tariff waiver for Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) and canceled its Validated End-User program. This means TSMC and similar companies will now require a special license to export chipmaking technology to China, aiming to level the playing field with U.S.-owned fabricators. President Trump also announced new tariffs on semiconductors from companies that do not produce them domestically, encouraging U.S. manufacturing.

title: Nvidia insists it isn’t Enron, but its AI deals are testing investor faith
summary: Nvidia's extensive partnerships in the AI sector, including vendor financing-like arrangements with companies like OpenAI and CoreWeave, are raising concerns among investors despite the company's surging stock price. While Nvidia vehemently denies comparisons to past corporate scandals like Enron or Lucent, critics argue that the circular nature of these deals and reliance on special-purpose vehicles could expose the company to significant risk if AI growth slows, potentially leading to write-downs and impacting its financial health. The company maintains that its transparent dealings and the vast potential of the AI market will ensure its continued success.

title: Nvidia hopes to ship first H200 GPUs to China by February, report claims
summary: Nvidia plans to ship its initial H200 GPUs to China by mid-February, with shipments ranging from 5,000 to 10,000 chip modules. This move follows U.S. President Donald Trump's approval, representing a significant policy shift from the previous administration's ban, although Chinese government approval for domestic companies to purchase remains outstanding. The policy change has sparked scrutiny from lawmakers concerned about the chips' military potential and impact on China's domestic chipmaking efforts.

title: NVIDIA at 41x Forward Earnings: Buy, Hold, or Cash Out?
summary: This article analyzes NVIDIA's current valuation at 41x forward earnings, considering both potential risks like trade wars and competition, and strong growth drivers. It concludes that despite its high P/E ratio, NVIDIA's robust growth outlook, easing trade tensions, and increasing data center spending make it an attractive investment with a "Strong Buy" Zacks Rank.

title: Nvidia debuts the Groq 3 language processing unit, a dedicated inference chip for multi-agent workloads
summary: Nvidia introduced the Groq 3 Language Processing Unit (LPU) at its GTC 2026 developer conference, a specialized chip designed for AI inference and multi-agent workloads. This LPU, stemming from a $20 billion deal to license Groq Inc.'s technology, focuses on high-speed memory and low-latency processing, complementing Nvidia's general-purpose GPUs. The Groq 3 is offered in dedicated LPX server racks, aiming to significantly enhance throughput for agentic systems and boost Nvidia's data center revenue amidst increasing demand for powerful compute performance.

title: Lowe Brockenbrough & Co. Inc. Grows Position in NVIDIA Corporation $NVDA
summary: Lowe Brockenbrough & Co. Inc. increased its stake in NVIDIA Corporation by 5.6% to 198,305 shares, valued at approximately $37 million, making it their 12th largest holding. This comes amidst strong financial performance by NVIDIA, including beating EPS and revenue expectations, and a consensus "Buy" rating from analysts with an average target price of $273.41. Despite significant institutional buying, company insiders have sold roughly 1.6 million shares over the last quarter.
